newsitem.title: MALTA: IMF tells Malta its budget is "not tough enough".
newsitem.headline: IMF tells Malta its budget is "not tough enough".

text.p: Maltese Prime Minister Alfred Sant said on Friday that an International Monetary Fund delegation had told his government the budget presented on January 13 was not tough enough given the country's economic situation.

Sant told parliament the IMF had concluded a confidential report about Malta by declaring: "The positive prospect of the medium-term outlook is...clouded by the emergence of large fiscal and external imbalances in recent years that if not quickly tackled could produce increased economic turbulence and imperil growth prospects."

The IMF also said: "The borrowing need of the public sector is likely to have reached 12 percent of GDP in 1996, up from 3.7 percent in 1992/93, reflecting both a weakening budgetary position and a deteriorating financial performance in public enterprises."
Sant said that despite the IMF's remarks, the government had decided to tackle the financial hole gradually.
"We do not want to burden the people with the consequences of the mistaken policies of the former government. Nor do we want to shock the economy," he said.

Finance Minister Lino Spiteri, presenting the new Labour government's first budget, had said the budgetary gap rose to 112 million Maltese pounds ($302.4m) in 1996 from a projected 38.9 million Maltese pounds.
